title: Payer Allowance Table for Insulin Pump Program Cartridge Notices
content:
For a cartridge or reservoir liability notice on an Insulin Pump Program, the allowance — the cartridges per 30 days the payer is expected to pay — follows the newest authorization grant for the item:

| Newest authorization grant for the item | Effect on the standard allowance |
|---|---|
| a payer prior authorization | replaced with its units authorized times 30, divided by the days its span covers with both ends included, rounded down |
| a grant resting on the written order itself, with an over-limit justification record dated in the 12 months before today on file | replaced with the quantity per 30 days on the written order it rests on |
| any other grant | the standard allowance stands |

The newest grant is the item's authorization grant with the latest valid-from date. An over-limit justification record is a clinical document recorded on the program for the purpose of over-limit justification, dated by its visit date. A record counts as in a number of months before today when its date is later than the same day of the month that many months before today, so a record dated exactly that many months before today is outside the window.

**Worked figures (hypothetical):** a prior authorization of 180 cartridges for a 182-day span gives 5,400 divided by 182, which is 29.67, rounded down to 29 per 30 days; a written-order grant on an order of 14 per 30 days with an over-limit justification record dated 3 months ago gives 14.
